newsitem.title: USA: UBS Securities adjusts Latam equity weightings.
newsitem.headline: UBS Securities adjusts Latam equity weightings.

text.p: UBS Securities said on Wednesday it was adjusting the recommended weightings in its model Latin American stock portfolio, trimming Argentina, Mexico and Peru while raising Venezuela, Brazil and Chile.
Argentina slipped to 11.5 percent from 12 percent in the portfolio, UBS said. Mexico dropped to 33.4 percent from 35 percent and Peru dipped to 2.5 percent from 3.0 percent.

Venezeula rose to 2.3 percent from 0.5 percent and Brazil rose to 36.8 percent from 34 percent. Chile was upped to 11 percent from 10 percent while Columbia remained at 2.5 percent, the brokerage said.
The previous model, set September 17, included three percent cash.
Lawrence Krohn, managing director, UBS Latin American Economics/Equity Strategy, said in the report that Argentina's weighting in the portfolio moved to market weight from overweight.

"We had overweighted Argentina for most of 1996," the report said. "Fiscal and labor problems will not disappear, and the market is historically vulnerable to a backup in U.S. bond yields, which UBS now expects."

Mexico was maintained at overweight, with the trimming of the recommended weight relative to that of September due to a change in market capitalization rather than any fundamental change, the report said.
Peru stayed at underweight. "Our underweight is not a function of the hostage crisis, but rather the failure of the economy to register lower inflation and narrower trade deficits," UBS said.

Venezuela was boosted to market weight from underweight, mostly due to an increase in market capitalization, rather than a significant improvement UBS's outlook on the country's fundamentals, the report said.
Brazil went to overweight from market weight. "President (Fernando Henrique) Cardoso, architect of the successful Real Plan, now seems likely to govern through 2002," UBS said.

UBS listed Colombia as underweight, from a previous market weight. "Our underweight reflects our perception that recent stability is somewhat illusory, masking economic imbalances (fiscal, commercial, monetary) that the recent emergency measures may not succeed in redressing."
The weightings measure UBS's recommended allocations relative the benchmark weightings set by the World Bank's International Finance Corp's so-called "investable" portfolio, Krohn said.
